miniProject.title: Installable taskrunner package with a typed registry and two seeded defects
miniProject.brief: Start the one repository the whole stage builds on: a src-layout taskrunner package that registers typed tasks, streams its run log lazily and cleans up run directories on every path. Install its wheel into a clean environment, then seed an aliasing defect and an object-lifetime defect, diagnose each and keep a regression test that fails on the seeded code.
steps: Run uv init --package taskrunner: uv 0.11.32 writes a src layout, the uv_build backend and the console script taskrunner = "taskrunner:main". Build the sdist and wheel with uv build, install the wheel into a new virtual environment outside the repository, and run taskrunner from another directory. Print taskrunner.__file__ from that environment to show the installed copy was imported, not src/.

Model a task as a frozen slotted dataclass TaskSpec(name, timeout_s, retries) whose __post_init__ rejects a name that is not an identifier, a timeout that is not positive and negative retries. Test an asdict round trip, a replace() change and use as a dict key. Define a Task Protocol for callables that take a params mapping and return a result dict, and a @task(name, timeout_s=..., retries=...) decorator factory that registers the function under its name and rejects duplicates.

Type the package under mypy --strict. If the decorator is typed to return the Task Protocol, mypy 2.4.0 rejects count_lines.__name__ on a decorated function, because the Protocol declares only __call__. A generic def task[F: Task](...) -> Callable[[F], F] that returns the function unchanged keeps its own type and metadata; keep both versions in the write-up.

Write the run log as JSON Lines, one record per run (task, params, status, seconds). Read it with a generator iter_runs(path) that parses one line at a time, and build the summary from generator expressions. With tracemalloc, compare the peak of summarizing through iter_runs against a version that first builds a list of records, at two log sizes such as 100,000 and 1,000,000 lines. Predict which peak grows with the file before measuring.

Give each run a directory through a @contextmanager run_dir(root, run_id) that yields the path, writes a done or failed marker and closes the run log on success, on task failure and on an exception raised inside the with block. Map failures to a small hierarchy (TaskError, ConfigError) and to CLI exit codes (0 success, 2 bad configuration, 3 task failure), raise each mapped error from its cause, and test that __cause__ survives.

Seed an aliasing defect: build each run's params with dict(DEFAULTS) and let a task extend params['paths']. The copy is shallow and shares the nested list, so with DEFAULTS = {'retries': 2, 'paths': ['data/in']} a run that adds 'extra' leaves the next run, and DEFAULTS itself, with ['data/in', 'extra']. Write the regression test first (two runs, then assert the second run and DEFAULTS are unchanged), watch it fail, and fix it with copy.deepcopy or immutable defaults, explaining the choice.

Seed a lifetime defect: a Runner that opens its log, closes it in __del__ and stores the bound method self.on_done = self._close_log. The instance holds the method and the method holds the instance, so with gc.disable() a del leaves the log open. Keep the probe as diagnosis evidence: a weakref callback has not fired after del, then gc.collect() returns a nonzero count (2 on CPython 3.14.4 for a runner holding only the log and the method), the log closes and the callback fires. The regression test deletes a runner with the collector disabled and asserts the log is closed. It fails on the seeded code, and still fails if a weakref.finalize is added while the bound method stays on the instance; it passes once on_done is the weakref.finalize(self, self.log.close) object itself, which holds no strong reference to the instance and runs at most once.
deliverables: The taskrunner repository: src-layout package, sdist and wheel, and a README with the clean-environment install commands and the taskrunner.__file__ output.
Tests for TaskSpec validation and round trip, duplicate registration, iter_runs laziness, run_dir cleanup on all three paths and exception causes, with mypy --strict reporting no issues.
Two defect write-ups, aliasing and lifetime, each with the failing regression output on the seeded code, the diagnosis evidence and the passing run after the fix.
The tracemalloc peak table for the lazy and list-building summaries at two log sizes, with the Python version.

rubric.pass: The wheel installs into a fresh environment and the taskrunner entry point runs from outside the repository with no sys.path edits.
rubric.strong: The README rebuilds and reinstalls from a clean clone in one copied block, and a test asserts the imported module is not under src/.

rubric.pass: TaskSpec rejects bad values, round-trips through asdict and works as a dict key; duplicates are rejected; mypy --strict reports no issues.
rubric.strong: Decorated tasks keep their own type, and the write-up shows the Protocol-typed decorator that mypy rejected and why.

rubric.pass: run_dir closes the log and writes its marker on success, failure and an inner raise, and mapped errors keep __cause__.
rubric.strong: The tracemalloc table shows the iter_runs peak staying flat while the list-building peak grows with the log.

rubric.pass: Both regression tests fail on the seeded code and pass after the fix.
rubric.strong: Each write-up names the reference behind the bug (the shared nested list; the method cycle) and why the fix removes it, for example why a finalizer added beside the bound method still needs a collector run.

miniProject.feedsInto: Capstone package and interface: the installable typed package, its entry point and the run log the service and pipeline write. Native and diagnosis: the lifetime write-up is a first evidence-first debugging report.
